Title: Those Who Understand: Knowledge Growth in Teaching
Key_Finding: Effective teaching requires pedagogical content knowledge: subject matter must be transformed into representations, examples, explanations, and sequences that novices can learn from.
Population: Conceptual paper on teaching knowledge; teacher education and classroom instruction

Authors: Mitchell J. Nathan; Anthony J. Petrosino
Title: Expert Blind Spot Among Preservice Teachers
Key_Finding: Greater subject-matter expertise was associated with less accurate judgments about novice difficulty; more mathematically advanced preservice teachers were more likely to mis-sequence algebra for beginners.

Title: How Effective Are Instructional Explanations in Example-Based Learning? A Meta-Analytic Review
Key_Finding: Adding instructional explanations to worked examples produced only a small overall gain, but explanations were more beneficial for conceptual understanding than for transfer.
Effect_Size: d=0.16 overall; d=0.36 for conceptual knowledge
Population: Students in example-based learning studies across multiple domains

Authors: Christina Areizaga Barbieri; Dana Miller-Cotto; Sarah N. Clerjuste; Kamal Chawla
Title: A Meta-analysis of the Worked Examples Effect on Mathematics Performance
Key_Finding: Worked examples improved mathematics performance versus comparison conditions, with correct worked examples outperforming incorrect-example formats; adding self-explanation prompts was not a reliable upgrade in this synthesis.
Population: Mathematics learners from elementary school to postsecondary education

Authors: Min Young Doo; Curtis J. Bonk; Heeok Heo
Title: A Meta-Analysis of Scaffolding Effects in Online Learning in Higher Education
Journal: The International Review of Research in Open and Distributed Learning
Key_Finding: Scaffolding improved online higher-education learning outcomes, with metacognitive scaffolds and some scaffold sources producing the largest gains.
Population: Higher-education students in online learning studies (64 effect sizes from 18 articles)

Authors: Mingzhang Zuo; Sen Kong; Yuxia Ma; Yue Hu; Meng Xiao
Title: The Effects of Using Scaffolding in Online Learning: A Meta-Analysis
Key_Finding: Across online-learning studies, scaffolding improved performance with a medium overall effect, and conceptual scaffolds outperformed strategic scaffolds.
Population: Students in online learning studies across grade levels and disciplines (83 effect sizes from 32 articles)

Authors: Philip J. Guo; Juho Kim; Rob Rubin
Title: How Video Production Affects Student Engagement: An Empirical Study of MOOC Videos
Journal: Proceedings of the First ACM Conference on Learning @ Scale Conference
Key_Finding: In large-scale MOOC logs, shorter and more personal-feeling videos were associated with substantially higher engagement than long, lecture-style recordings.
Population: MOOC learners on edX (6.9 million video-watching sessions)

Authors: René F. Kizilcec; Jeremy N. Bailenson; Charles J. Gomez
Title: The Instructor's Face in Video Instruction: Evidence From Two Large-Scale Field Studies
Key_Finding: Showing the instructor’s face strategically rather than constantly changed learner experience, but did not improve learning outcomes or attrition in a 10-week field experiment.
Population: Online learners in two field studies, including a 10-week experiment (N=12,468) and an 8-week observational study (N=2,951)

Title: Effects of Instructor-Present Videos on Learning, Cognitive Load, Motivation, and Social Presence: A Meta-Analysis
Key_Finding: Across experimental studies, instructor-present videos did not improve learning or social presence overall, but they did increase motivation and cognitive load.
Population: Learners in 20 experimental studies of instructional videos

Authors: Maik Beege; Noah L. Schroeder; Steffi Heidig; Günter Daniel Rey; Sascha Schneider
Title: The Instructor Presence Effect and Its Moderators in Instructional Video: A Series of Meta-Analyses
Key_Finding: A visible instructor produced a small benefit for retention but not transfer, while reliably increasing social presence, motivation, and affective ratings.
Effect_Size: g+=0.22 for retention; g+=0.06 for transfer
Population: Learners in 35 studies, 46 pairwise comparisons, 6,339 participants

Title: The Effectiveness of Enhanced Interaction Features in Educational Videos: A Meta-Analysis
Key_Finding: Educational videos with meaningful interaction features such as embedded questions or tasks outperformed videos with only navigational features or no interactivity; not pausing for the interaction impaired learning.
Population: Learners in 17 studies (22 effect sizes) of educational videos

Authors: Fabienne M. van der Kleij; Remco C. W. Feskens; Theo J. H. M. Eggen
Title: Effects of Feedback in a Computer-Based Learning Environment on Students’ Learning Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis
Key_Finding: Elaborated feedback outperformed correctness-only feedback and answer-only feedback in computer-based environments, especially for higher-order outcomes.
Population: Students in computer-based learning studies (40 studies, 70 effect sizes)

Authors: Benedikt Wisniewski; Klaus Zierer; John Hattie
Title: The Power of Feedback Revisited: A Meta-Analysis of Educational Feedback Research
Key_Finding: Feedback produced a medium overall positive effect on learning, but effectiveness varied substantially by the information content of the feedback.

Authors: Ute Mertens; Bridgid Finn; Marlit Annalena Lindner
Title: Effects of Computer-Based Feedback on Lower- and Higher-Order Learning Outcomes: A Network Meta-Analysis
Key_Finding: Elaborated feedback ranked as the most effective computer-based feedback type for both lower-order and higher-order outcomes, outperforming KR and KCR feedback.
Effect_Size: g=0.71 for lower-order outcomes; g=0.46 for higher-order outcomes
Population: Learners in 77 experimental studies (163 effect sizes)

Authors: Johanna Fleckenstein; Lucas W. Liebenow; Jennifer Meyer
Title: Automated Feedback and Writing: A Multi-Level Meta-Analysis of Effects on Students' Performance
Key_Finding: Automated writing feedback improved writing performance with a medium overall effect, but results varied substantially by implementation and study context.
Population: Students using automated writing evaluation tools (20 studies, k=84, N=2,828)

Authors: Louis Alfieri; Timothy J. Nokes-Malach; Christian D. Schunn
Title: Learning Through Case Comparisons: A Meta-Analytic Review
Key_Finding: Case comparison activities improved learning over alternatives, especially when learners compared for common structure and received principles after the comparison.

Title: Motivation in Online Learning: Testing a Model of Self-Determination Theory
Key_Finding: In online certificate programs, need satisfaction mediated the link between contextual support and learner motivation, but motivation did not directly predict learning outcomes in the tested model.
Population: Adult learners in two online certificate programs (N=262)

Authors: Yurou Wang; Hui Wang; Shengnan Wang; Stefanie A. Wind; Christopher Gill
Title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Self-Determination-Theory-Based Interventions in the Education Context
Key_Finding: SDT-based educational interventions increased autonomy and competence support outcomes and produced a positive effect on intrinsic motivation in experimental and quasi-experimental studies.
Population: Students across school and university settings in 36 intervention studies; 31 studies contributed effect sizes
